questions.q: In this lab, which operation actually changes the trainable weights?
choices: model.train()
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()
optimizer.zero_grad()
questions.why: backward computes and accumulates gradients; the optimizer step uses them to update parameters. The mode setter and gradient reset do not apply weight updates.

questions.q: What should F.cross_entropy receive for ordinary integer next-token targets?
choices: Raw logits and integer target IDs
Softmax probabilities as logits and integer target IDs
Generated text and training text
Argmax token IDs and probabilities
questions.why: The function performs logarithmic normalization internally. Passing probabilities as logits changes the objective. This question concerns hard target IDs, not the separate soft-label API.

questions.q: For unweighted mean cross entropy over N positions with hard targets, what is the gradient with respect to each logit row?
choices: The logits divided by N
N times the probability-minus-one-hot vector
The one-hot target minus probability, with no scaling
Probability minus the one-hot target, divided by N
questions.why: Mean reduction divides every position's contribution by N. This formula is for logits; earlier parameter gradients still require the chain rule.

questions.q: Why does the loop normally reset gradients before a new update?
choices: To erase the old learned weights
Because backward adds to gradient buffers that may contain an earlier update's derivatives
Because evaluation otherwise changes vocabulary size
To reset AdamW's entire optimizer state
questions.why: The reset affects temporary gradient buffers, not learned weights or optimizer moment state. Intentional microbatch accumulation uses a different, explicitly scaled reset schedule.

questions.q: The alternating-pattern training loss falls while the repeated-zero stress loss rises. What is justified?
choices: The model generalizes better to all inputs
PyTorch's backward operation is broken
Training fit improved, but the deliberately different stress distribution became less well predicted
The stress example proves natural-language overfitting at a particular epoch
questions.why: The experiment is a controlled distribution mismatch. It disproves a blanket generalization claim but is not an independently sampled language evaluation or an ordinary overfitting study.

questions.q: The hand example starts at logits [0, 0, 0], target index 1, and gradient [1/3, -2/3, 1/3]. With plain SGD learning rate 0.3, what are the new logits and what happens to the target probability?
questions.answer: The new logits are [-0.1, 0.2, -0.1]. The target probability rises from one third to 0.402960; loss falls from 1.098612 to 0.908918 in the recorded run.
questions.why: Subtract learning rate times gradient. The target's negative derivative raises its logit. These are the measured Part 1 results, not an AdamW update.

questions.q: Set the Part 4 learning rate to 0.0 while keeping zero-initialized logits and weight_decay=0.0. What happens to the bigram weights and training loss after the loop?
questions.answer: Weights remain zero and the training loss stays ln(8), displayed as 2.079442. Forward, backward and gradient resets can still execute.
questions.why: Computing derivatives is not itself a weight update. A zero learning rate prevents the parameter changes in this setup; the initial uniform-loss value comes from the lab and zero-rate behavior is unit-tested.

questions.q: Explain the complete next-token training loop, including input-target alignment, raw logits, backward, gradient reset and the limit of a falling training curve.
rubric: Targets are the following tokens, produced by a one-position shift, not copies of inputs
The forward pass produces vocabulary logits; cross entropy compares them with integer targets
Backward accumulates derivatives in gradient buffers and does not itself update weights
Normally clear prior gradients before the new backward; the optimizer step changes registered parameters
Training loss describes fit to the measured objective and examples, not proof of generalization, truth or agent safety

questions.q: An engineer splits a batch into unequal microbatches, averages each microbatch's mean loss equally, and expects the full-batch mean gradient. Diagnose the error and explain how to obtain the intended update.
rubric: Equal weighting of unequal-sized means gives individual targets different effective weights
Scale each microbatch mean by its contributing target count divided by the total count
Clear gradients once, accumulate those scaled backwards at unchanged weights, then take one optimizer step
Taking an optimizer step after each microbatch changes the weights used by later gradients and is a different procedure
The exact equivalence assumes the same per-example computation; stochastic or batch-dependent layers can complicate comparisons

recall.q: What does backward change, and what does optimizer.step change?
recall.a: Backward accumulates gradient buffers. In this training loop, the optimizer step changes trainable parameters using those gradients.

recall.q: What goes into PyTorch cross entropy for hard next-token labels?
recall.a: Raw vocabulary logits and integer target IDs. Do not apply softmax to the input first.

recall.q: How do inputs and targets align for the GPT in this project?
recall.a: Inputs are tokens[:, :-1], targets are tokens[:, 1:]. The model does not shift the targets internally.

recall.q: How does eval mode differ from no_grad?
recall.a: Eval changes layer behavior such as dropout. no_grad disables recording the differentiation graph for the enclosed computations. Neither is an optimizer update.

recall.q: What does a lower training loss prove?
recall.a: Improved fit on the measured training objective and examples, not useful behavior on arbitrary new inputs. Use appropriate independent evaluation for broader claims.

recall.q: What is the unweighted hard-target mean cross-entropy logit gradient?
recall.a: For each position, (probability minus one-hot target) divided by the number of scored positions. Earlier parameter gradients require chaining through the model.
